For the divisor count, I can show you the formula!

When a number is expressed in prime factorization as:
$$n = p_1^{a_1} \cdot p_2^{a_2} \cdot p_3^{a_3} \cdots p_k^{a_k}$$

The number of divisors is:
$$\tau(n) = (a_1 + 1)(a_2 + 1)(a_3 + 1) \cdots (a_k + 1)$$

For your bunny's bouquet with $2^4 \cdot 3^3 \cdot 5^2 \cdot 7^2$:

$$\tau(n) = (4+1)(3+1)(2+1)(2+1)$$
$$= 5 \cdot 4 \cdot 3 \cdot 3$$
$$= 180$$

**The bunny can label 180 different little bunches by their divisors!** What a lovely detail for a picture book—readers could even try finding some of the divisor combinations themselves. 🐰🌸
